description: The pair layer's isospin parity is inverted and bring_color_weighted cannot repair it. The charge-antisymmetric (isovector) part of the like-pair channel is h/2, forced exactly by the Hecke skein relation sigma - sigma^-1 = q - 1/q under p |-> positive crossing, n |-> negative crossing. The charge-symmetric T=0/T=1 splitting is h*delta/4 under bring_color_weighted and exactly zero under strict_averaged. The isovector term is 1454x the isoscalar one; nuclear physics wants the reverse. bring_color_weighted modifies only the p-n factor, which is self-conjugate and therefore already charge-even, so it does not touch the term that is wrong.
convention: D (z = q^3/(q^2+1)), canonical per owner ruling R1 2026-08-15

assertions.name: f_pp - f_nn == h exactly -- the isovector term IS the skein relation
so the odd part is exactly h/2, with no free coefficient
bring_color_weighted leaves f_pp and f_nn untouched, so O is identical under every pn_convention
the T=0/T=1 splitting under bring is exactly h*delta/4
under strict_averaged the T=0/T=1 splitting is exactly zero
the isovector term exceeds the isoscalar splitting by > 1000x
the model's mirror asymmetry has the right SIGN (3H more bound)
and overshoots the observed A=3 splitting by more than 2x

scope: (a) for the physics judgement -- charge symmetry is an empirical near-symmetry, not a theorem about this model, so 'the parity is inverted' is an observation against experiment, not a proved exclusion. EXACT and unconditional for the algebra: f_pp - f_nn = h identically, and bring_color_weighted leaves it unchanged. Those two are what constrain any repair -- the isovector term cannot be reduced by choosing a different pn_convention, only by changing the p/n-to-crossing-sign identification itself. Nothing wired to production; nothing refuted.
